<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Digging deeper into critical areas for Linux-specific assumptions.

Node.js glob path separators on Windows are being checked. Minimatch fails on backslash paths by default. cli.ts uses `file://` comparisons that break on Windows. Coverage thresholds expect `src/`. Bun shell handles `rm -rf` and `AGENT=1`. Next: config.test.ts.

Bun's internal shell is POSIX-like and cross-platform, so `&&`, `rm -rf`, and `AGENT=1` often work on Windows. Breakage only occurs under `npm run` or direct `cmd.exe` execution. PowerShell 7+ supports `&&`, but `AGENT=1` does not. A relative path concatenation bug (`relative + "/target.ts"`) was also found.

</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Noticed a potential cross-platform import issue where `./src\\rules\\all-rules.ts` uses backslashes, which may cause problems on Unix-like systems.

The backslash import works from the project root via `bun -e`, but fails when executed from inside `src/rules/` because the relative path resolves to `src/rules/src/rules/all-rules.ts`. The `isRuleFile` check also misses these files since their basenames contain backslashes.

Windows backslashes break the rule-file detection logic. The `startsWith('all-rules')` check fails on Windows because the basename contains the full path rather than just the filename. This causes all files to be misclassified as rule files. The `INFRA_FILES` check also breaks because it compares against the full path instead of the filename. This is a significant Windows test breakage.

Coverage thresholds break on Windows because Bun emits backslashes in filenames like `src\assertions.ts`, while the regex expects forward slashes (`src/`). The check never matches any lines, so coverage gates silently pass even with low coverage. This is a severe Windows breakage.

</details></think>

